rows.en: Inside the New Federation
rows.notes: Archive topic 3; width limit of the archive list unknown to me.

rows.en: <library(1)><operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>While we are at it, it seems best that we explain who we are to you.

<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>Me, <color(4)>Jamil<ce()>, <color(4)>Gain Bijou<ce()>, and <color(4)>Hayato Jin<ce()> - the four of us<thumbnail(178)> - are each hostile to the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()>.
rows.notes: 'Hayato Jin' for 'Jin Hayato' (Japanese name order) per character_names_021.json.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>We're cooperating with each other, each for our own goal, and fighting the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()>.
<operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>The <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> is a unified government headed by <book(40)>Fixx Bloodman<endbook()><thumbnail(179)>.
rows.notes: 'Fixx Bloodman' per encyclopedia_021_a/022 locked spelling for book(40) (not 'Fix Bradman').

rows.en: <operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>The <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()>'s true goal is hegemony over the Earth Sphere - its long-held wish since the old Federation's days.
rows.notes: Orchestrator: shortened to fit three lines.

rows.en: <operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>To that end, they are scheming to turn unknown powers such as Newtypes and the <book(48)>Shin Dragon<endbook()> to military use.
<thumbdown()><operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>Such foolish conduct must absolutely be stopped.
<library(2)><topic()><operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>I was surprised you came from another world, but you really don't seem to know a thing. Let me give you a short history rundown.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>This world has seen as many as seven wars fought in the past.

<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>Getter Robo, developed by Dr. <color(5)>Saotome<ce()>, drove off the <book(49)>Invaders<endbook()> that had appeared on the Moon - the <book(53)>Moon Invader War<endbook()><thumbnail(180)>.
rows.notes: Restructured as a label ending in the named event, mirroring the source's own fragment structure; book(53) matches encyclopedia_022's locked title 'Moon Invader War' even though the source here writes the short form 'the lunar war' inside the tag.

rows.en: <operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>After that, Dr. <color(5)>Saotome<ce()> started a rebellion and built the <book(48)>Shin Dragon<endbook()>, which he called the ultimate Getter.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>To destroy it, fanatical top brass ended up firing the <book(52)>Deuteron Missile<endbook()>, a weapon strong enough to half-destroy Earth.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>At the same time, the "Summer of Love" - a mass outbreak of <book(70)>Trapar<endbook()><thumbnail(181)> - occurred.

<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>At the time, the leading authority on <book(69)>Scub<endbook()> research, studying the <book(61)>Nirvash<endbook()> and <color(4)>Eureka<ce()>, was <book(68)>Adroc Thurston<endbook()>.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>In exchange for his own life, he held the damage from all this to a minimum, and he's regarded as the hero who saved the world.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>That very <book(68)>Adroc<endbook()> is <color(4)>Renton<ce()>'s father.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>And then... the 7th Space War broke out - the final war between Earth and the colonies.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>The <book(42)>Space Rev. Army<endbook()> issued the Earth Federation a demand to surrender, backed by a colony drop.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>In response, the Earth Federation deployed its decisive weapon, the <book(37)>Gundam X<endbook()><thumbnail(182)>...
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>But the operation went through, and countless colonies were dropped on Earth.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>The colony drops wrecked the environment, blocking sunlight from the surface. Earth's population fell to as low as one-fifth.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>After that, <book(69)>Scub Coral<endbook()> gradually formed the land, and the environment began to regenerate.

<thumbdown()><operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>And even now, that war is on the verge of repeating itself - at the hands of the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> and the <book(42)>Space Rev. Army<endbook()>.
<library(3)><topic()><operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>I believe I've already told you that you, the <color(4)>Nadesico<ce()>, have been marked by the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()>, but...
<operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>It seems word is circulating that you are assassins sent by the <book(42)>Space Rev. Army<endbook()><thumbnail(184)>.
<operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>Because of this, the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> is on high alert internally too - the colony side is the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()>'s natural enemy.
<thumbdown()><operator(30080,1)><speed(2)>I do not know why such false information is being spread, but... there seems to be something behind it.

uncertainties.issue: Archive topic titles ('Vulture' / 'Recent Circumstances' / 'Inside the New Federation'): width limit of the archive list screen is unknown to me, as in the reviewed 4003962/4003942.
<thumbnail(178)> attaches to 'the four [of us]' after all four names in the source; kept at the same relative point after the name list in English.

Restructured this label-style row to lead with the cause and end with the named event, keeping book(53) and its thumbnail last as in the source; book(53) rendered 'Moon Invader War' (its locked encyclopedia title) even though this row's own tag text is the shorter 'lunar war'.
Kept the source's clause order (Scub research -> Nirvash/Eureka -> Adroc Thurston named last) via a 'was' construction, to preserve book-span order without inventing facts.

checked_decisions: Slots 0-2 archive topic titles: the 128-visible-char screen-title limit (per this task's brief) applies here too; all three titles ('Vulture', 'Recent Circumstances', 'Inside the New Federation') are far under it, so the translator's 'width limit unknown' uncertainty is resolved - no fix needed.

Slot 20 'Hayato Jin' name order and thumbnail(178) placement checked against source (right after the '4 persons' phrase); thumbnail kept at the same point; accepted. Speaker is Holland Novak (30110), so 'Me' = Holland, and the named three (Jamil, Gain Bijou, Hayato Jin) plus Holland total four; consistent.
Slot 22 'Fixx Bloodman' confirmed locked spelling (encyclopedia_021_a.json / encyclopedia_022.json).

Slot 28 ruling applied: book(53) rendered 'Moon Invader War' accepted per this task's ruling; confirmed as the locked encyclopedia_022.json title, reused correctly even though this row's own source text uses the shorter (lunar war) form.

Slot 32 'Adroc Thurston' confirmed locked spelling (encyclopedia_021_b.json/022.json note 'Adroc' per Eureka Seven wiki, 'Adrock' is a rejected Wikipedia variant); clause-order restructuring to end on his name (matching the source's label structure) accepted, no invented facts.

Slots 27-41 (Talho Yuki's history rundown) checked against source line-by-line: Getter Robo/Moon Invader War, Shin Dragon rebellion, Deuteron Missile, Summer of Love/Trapar outbreak, Adroc Thurston/Nirvash/Eureka research, 7th Space War, Space Rev. Army colony-drop ultimatum, Gundam X deployment, population loss to one-fifth (20%), Scub Coral land regeneration, and the closing 'war about to repeat' line all match; no reversed meaning or invented subject found.

Slots 42-45 (Sala Tyrrell) checked against source: Nadesico marked by New Federation, false assassin rumor from Space Rev. Army, New Federation's internal alert status, and 'something behind it' all match.
No lowercase j/q outside locked names ('Jamil', 'Bijou', 'Jin' all capitalized/part of locked names); verified by script.
remaining_uncertainties: Slot 28: the source places the sentence-ending period before <thumbnail(180)>, while the English places the period after the tag (both after book(53)/endbook()); command list and order are identical, this is a one-character punctuation/tag-adjacency difference only, not a meaning issue, but noting it since it's a call on tag placement.
Slot 32: clause order (Scub research -> Nirvash/Eureka -> Adroc Thurston named last) rebuilt with a 'was' construction to preserve book-span order without inventing facts; kept.
